Requirements: 1. The text contains page numbers in square brackets, such as [01], [02], etc. - These must be passed through unchanged. - Each page number must appear in exactly the same position in the translation as in the source. - The number of page markers in the output must match the input exactly.
2. Personal names, place names, titles, and other proper nouns should be rendered in Hànyǔ Pīnyīn with tone marks.
3. Do NOT transcribe the full Classical Chinese text into Pinyin.
4. Do NOT include explanatory notes, annotations, or commentary — output only the $lang translation.
5. The target language is $lang.

"The Dharma of the self-mind is formless,
From the First Patriarch Śākyamuni onward,
not a single patriarch did not silently realize and self-verify it.
Therefore, Bodhidharma directly pointed without establishing words,
merely facing the wall for nine years at Shàolín.
Even when the Second Patriarch stood in snow and severed his arm,
not a single word was spoken to him.
Only his erroneous views were negated,
and thus the Second Patriarch attained correct knowledge and vision,
So, the Second Patriarch did not enter through Bodhidharma's words or phrases but self-verified it.
Moreover, Bǎizhàng rolling up the mat,
ancient virtues have shown people in many such ways,
precisely because it does not lie in words or phrases.
If even words and phrases are like this,
how much more so with written texts?
The essence of the Mind School must be personally contemplated;
what have the patriarchs' words and phrases to do with us?"
Although the mind Dharma is said to be formless,
Frogs and earthworms trigger mechanisms; pipes and strings transmit the mind.
Even walls and tiles are all expounding the Dharma.
Thus, Língyún saw peach blossoms and awakened to the Way,
Xuánshā said speaking swallows deeply discuss true reality.
If so, then the entire earth is a gate to enlightenment;
How much more the words and phrases that clarify the Mind School?
How much more the texts that record the clarification of the Mind School?
If these two truly have nothing to do with the Mind School,
why did Jiànfú Gù read Yúnmén's record and awaken?
Why did Huánglóng Xīn read Duōfú's sayings and enlighten?
It is because verbal expressions are quiescent, and the nature of words is empty—
If through words, phrases, and texts,
one sees the emptiness and stillness of nature and characteristics,
that is a direct leap and immediate entry.
Therefore, I know that the circulation of this book
will enlighten many in their mind-ground.
Moreover, when Jiàn was seeking alms,
a commoner named Zhōu from Nínghǎi county in Tāizhōu sighed and said,
'In my land, there is a large pear tree,
which has passed through three generations.
In recent years, members of my family each had dreams
of pavilions and corridors upon it,
with countless monks coming and going among them.
I always wondered until now I realize—
it must be for carving this Record!'
So he donated it to make printing blocks,
and invited Jiàn to hire craftsmen at his home to carve them.
Zhōu dreamed of six monks requesting to see the carved blocks.
'These are the six generations of robe-transmitting patriarchs, specially coming to bear witness to this matter.'
Alas, this book serves as a great event;
thus, it is fitting to have auspicious responses that awaken people's minds.
Therefore, I record this together so that readers
may know it is no small affinity and strengthen their faith."

The matter of the Buddha's teachings lies in daily activities.
It is in your walking, standing, sitting, and lying down; in your drinking tea and eating meals; in your conversations and inquiries.
Yet, what you do and what you think are not it.
If you understand, you are the unhindered and free true person right now.
If you do not understand, you are a person bearing heavy crimes, carrying cangues and chains.
The Buddha's teachings are not far away, not separated by eons as numerous as dust and sand.
You see it in a single thought of yours.
It is on your eyebrows and nostrils.
If you do not see it,
it is like trying to catch the moon by joining bamboo poles—everywhere yet elusive.
Do not ponder it, nor speak of it.
At that moment, what grace do you rely on?
If you know this, you must have a place of joy.
All dharmas are originally without emotion,
All Buddhas are originally self-aware and spiritual.
Blending together like the great void, neither lacking nor surplus.
If not, you are simply obstructed at every turn.
Not knowing where this body ultimately lands, through vast eons, you only cling to things, attach to realms, and mistake forms as real.
Not abandoning affection, delusion, and attachment to wealth and treasures.
Establishing self, contending with others—a mass of willful energy.
With the slightest opposition, your face turns blue or red.
How could you know you are in the sea of karmic obstacles and the pit of sins?
Eating meat is like a hungry ghost devouring corpses,
Drinking alcohol like a starving dog lapping water,
Craving sensual pleasures like a thirsty fly sucking blood.
Unaware that this body is a great calamity, indulging ignorance and foolishly nurturing willfulness.
Soon it will decay, dying in vain and living emptily.
Vainly passing through thousands of kalpas, merely rising and falling aimlessly.
Why not recognize the diamond-solid body and the path of eternal life without extinction?
In this world, the head is stubborn,
When the impermanent killing ghost arrives at your bedside,
You still use your mind to cling to wealth and realms.
Suddenly driven away to see King Yánluó,
Unable to utter a word, the iron furnace, fiery coals, copper pillars, and mountain of knives become your playthings.
At that time, regret is greatly difficult to avoid.
Now, while illness has not yet sought your body,
Why not, in the twelve hours of the day, seek even a hair's breadth of good benefit and prepare a bridge?
This illusory form—what can be relied upon as real?
The Buddhas of the past left sutras and composed treatises,
All wholesome dharmas are for you, beginners,
To repent sins, eliminate obstacles, and gradually increase benefits.
Seek a good-knowing advisor to reveal the Dharma gate of liberation.
In the nature of ignorance, recognize the true master.
Obtaining a human body through myriad kalpas is not easy.
Do you know that this body's original nature is simultaneous with the Buddha, originally without lack or deficiency?
There is one great matter in your urine bag and dung pile,
If you cannot believe, then you will forever fall into the deep pit and sea of sins.
If you turn the light around and reflect within,

Confusion, afflictions, ignorance, and wild passions instantly vanish.
All conditioned realms transform into sweet dew and the land of peace and bliss.

Hell and heaven also depend on your mind.
Right now, if you correspond, you unite with the Buddha.
Wisdom is the Buddha, with no deception.
Directly believe without doubt—the mind is true enlightenment.
Why must you pass through countless great kalpas?
This life is extremely difficult to encounter.
Do not say, "I am an ordinary person," and retreat or belittle yourself.

Not relying on the Buddha's teachings, all dharmas are deviant views and external paths.

Relying on this as real is not dependable.
Even the old masters in the assembly cannot help you.

You must exert your own effort; your future depends on yourself.
If you perform all conditioned meritorious deeds,

Seek offerings, day and night uneasy, concerned it may not be right.
Let me say to all directions,
The elders may laugh at me,
But they cannot blame this mountain monk.
